body:
Vanessa Ortiz: Heads up: readiness SLI emission for Dedicated pools is rolling out behind the flag this week (from the scheduler + capacity signal). Question we need to settle before we wire alerts: do we *page* on readiness dips, or start ticket-only? I’m seeing some expected “not-ready” blips during scale events and don’t want to wake people up for noise.

Rafael Mendes: +1 to being careful. What’s the current definition in the metric? is it “pool can accept new work” (i.e. admitted capacity) or “scheduler healthy” or both?

Vanessa Ortiz: both right now. `dedicated_pool_ready=1` only if (a) scheduler health OK and (b) capacity signal says we can admit at least N concurrent requests for that customer pool. If either fails -> 0.

Aisha Bello: ok that’s good for customer impact, but it’s also going to catch autoscaling lag, which is… often not customer-impacting if queue absorbs it.

Lauren Bishop: from a Dedicated customer POV, “pool not ready” reads like outage. If we page on every short dip, we’ll end up desensitized. I’d rather page when it correlates to actual 429/5xx or admission failures.

Sean Gallagher: principle I’m trying to keep us aligned on: page when we’re likely burning budget materially / customer impact imminent, ticket for everything else. Readiness is a great leading indicator but also likely noisy at first.

Sergio Costa: for alerting we could do burn-rate style on readiness SLI itself (multiwindow) vs simple threshold. But… we haven’t even locked target yet. Right now I can wire: 
- ticket: readiness < 99.5% over 30m
- page: readiness < 99.0% over 10m AND request rejects/overload > X

Miles Thornton: I like the “two-signal” gating. If readiness dips but we’re still serving (no reject spikes), page is probably wrong.

Keiko Yamamoto: fwiw, during scale-up we’ll see readiness flap as nodes register + KV warmup. A straight 5m threshold will false-positive. We can also add an annotation/label for “autoscaling_in_progress=1” to suppress/route as ticket.

Ethan Park: control plane side: we can emit an “admission blocked due to capacity” counter already. If we require that to be elevated for paging, we’ll avoid most of the warmup flaps.

Rafael Mendes: can we separate the SLI into two time series? `scheduler_ready` vs `capacity_ready`? Then page on scheduler readiness (more severe), ticket on capacity readiness until we tune.

Vanessa Ortiz: yes, that’s doable. The combined one was for “customer promise”, but I agree we need component metrics for debugging.

Aisha Bello: also we need to decide if readiness becomes part of the Dedicated tier SLO table *now* or stays “informational” until validation. If it’s in the SLO, it will immediately impact budget + enforcement.

Sean Gallagher: my vote: Phase 1 = informational + ticketing only. After 2-4 weeks of data + backtest, we can promote to SLO with a target and then revisit paging.

Lauren Bishop: +1. And for customers, we can message “readiness is an internal signal; your SLO is still availability/latency for requests.” We should not implicitly create a new external commitment via paging policy.

Sergio Costa: ok so operational plan:
1) Ship metrics (combined + components)
2) Dashboard panel + annotations for scale events
3) Alert rule ticket-only initially (to #eng-sre + Dedicated oncall inbox)
4) Page only if combined readiness is low *and* admission-blocked counter indicates rejects (or sustained 5xx)

Miles Thornton: what’s “low” for paging once enabled? I’d rather avoid a single 10m window. Something like: page when readiness burn rate > 14x on 1h/5m windows (or equivalent), i.e. it would consume monthly budget quickly.

Aisha Bello: +1 to burn rate. But we need a defined budget first. If we pick 99.9% monthly readiness, the budget is ~43m/month. A 5m outage is already noticeable but not necessarily page-worthy unless it’s impacting serving. Hence two-signal approach.

Rafael Mendes: also note Dedicated pools are per-customer; we should be careful about paging “Dedicated-oncall” for a single tenant blip that’s self-inflicted (traffic spike beyond commit). We need the exclusion story.

Vanessa Ortiz: good call. We *can* tag events where over-commit happens (requested > reserved + burst). That should be excluded from readiness SLI for SLO purposes, but we still might want an internal ticket.

Sean Gallagher: let’s write this down as policy for the rollout:
- Readiness SLI starts as “informational” and “ticket-only” for 2 weeks
- Paging condition requires (a) readiness drop sustained and (b) clear customer impact signal (admission blocked / elevated 5xx) and (c) not during planned autoscaling warmup unless impact present
- After validation, decide whether readiness is an SLO for Dedicated tier and set burn-rate thresholds accordingly

Sergio Costa: I’ll implement ticket-only rule first and add the “impact gate” logic behind a feature flag so we can turn paging on later without rewriting. Who owns the written criteria? Aisha + Vanessa?

Aisha Bello: yep, I can draft the criteria + exclusions section and link it to the Dedicated tier SLO notes. Vanessa, can you add the component metric plan + sample screenshots once it’s in staging?

Vanessa Ortiz: 👍 will do. I’ll also post a couple example traces of the autoscaling flap so people see what “expected” looks like.

Keiko Yamamoto: please include the scale event annotation in the dashboard. It’ll save us a ton of “why did readiness drop at 02:13” threads.

Lauren Bishop: and loop me on the customer-facing language so we don’t accidentally imply “pool readiness SLO” before we mean it.

Sean Gallagher: sounds good. Decision for now: **ticket-only for readiness dips**, paging only when coupled with clear admission impact, and we revisit after we have 2+ weeks of data. :thumbsup:

Sergio Costa: ack. I’ll route the ticket alert to the Dedicated oncall queue (not page) and include links to the readiness + admission panels.

Miles Thornton: once we have those tickets, I’ll help categorize: autoscaling warmup vs real scheduler degradation vs capacity fragmentation. That’ll inform the target + whether paging is even useful.

Vanessa Ortiz: thanks all. I’ll update when the metrics are live in prod.
